text: A feeling of isolation might emerge. <break time="0.8s" /> Which can easily develop into lonely silence. <break time="0.8s" /> If students cannot sense. <break time="0.8s" /> The presence of teachers and peers. <break time="0.8s" /> Including not seeing their faces. <break time="0.8s" /> Not knowing their backgrounds. <break time="0.8s" /> Not receiving any welcome activities. <break time="0.8s" /> Not being guided to interact. <break time="0.8s" /> And not understanding clearly what to do during a course of study. <break time="0.8s" /> A study by Duran on a graduate programme at a Canadian university. <break time="0.8s" /> Demonstrates that students do influence each other. <break time="0.8s" /> In behaviour. <break time="0.8s" /> If many students in a virtual class. <break time="0.8s" /> Seem too quiet. <break time="0.8s" /> Others might be influenced by this norm. <break time="0.8s" /> And instinctively practise it. <break time="0.8s" /> Research by Adams and van Manen also shows. <break time="0.8s" /> That students who try to share ideas without receiving any peer response. <break time="0.8s" /> Easily feel devalued. <break time="0.8s" /> And become reluctant to contribute again. <break time="0.8s" /> When articulate students in a class. <break time="0.8s" /> Frequently experience. <break time="0.8s" /> This unpleasant feeling of speaking to a wall. <break time="0.8s" /> They might end up being. <break time="0.8s" /> As silent as all the others. <break time="0.8s" /> When this happens. <break time="0.8s" /> And lasts for some time. <break time="0.8s" /> The atmosphere of the class would develop. <break time="0.8s" /> Into a collective inertia that is not easily mended.
